title: RTT replay header, version 2
description: The <stem>.json header of a v2 episode replay. Poses live in <stem>.bin with the v1 layout: little-endian float32 [frames x bodies x 7], each body frame's world pose (px, py, pz, qx, qy, qz, qw), Z up, metres. Bodies are drawn from content-addressed GLB assets placed in the body frame; v1-style primitive geoms are optional and serve as the collision overlay. Readers accept version 1 (the v1 header) and version 2 (this schema).
$comment: Rules JSON Schema cannot express, checked by rtt.studio.replay.check_lane_header and the tests (a plain float32 header without t, cuts or quantised, as the v1 writers make it, is still checked by rtt.sim.replay.check_header, which check_lane_header applies first): n_bodies == len(bodies); the .bin file holds n_frames * n_bodies * 7 float32 values (n_frames * n_bodies * 7 int16 words when quantised); t, when present, has one strictly increasing time per frame; cuts are strictly increasing frame indices below n_frames; every visual's asset is a key of assets and every asset is drawn by some visual (assets holds exactly the referenced entries); each asset key equals sha256[:16] and its uri equals 'assets/' + key + '.glb'; sha256 and bytes match the file; the overlay sidecar, when present, holds n_frames * len(channels) float16 values.

bin.description: File name of the pose sidecar, next to the header.

assets.description: Every asset the replay draws, keyed by asset id (sha256[:16] of the file). Entries are copied verbatim from the asset manifest.

bodies.description: One entry per posed body, in the order of the pose sidecar's body axis.

static_visuals.description: Assets placed in the world frame that never move (props).

t.description: Keyframed lanes: the time in seconds of every stored frame (one per frame), strictly increasing and not uniform. Without it frame i is at i / fps.

cuts.description: Frame indices where a new segment starts (a tool change or a head switch). There is a frame exactly at each segment start and a player never interpolates across a cut. Without it the lane has no cuts.

quantised.description: True: the .bin holds little-endian int16 [frames x bodies x 7] (dtype int16, pose_fields px py pz qa qb qc qi), frames then bodies in the header's order. A pose is [px, py, pz, qa, qb, qc, qi]: the position in units of 0.1 mm, round(mm * 10); the quaternion in smallest-three form: the component of largest magnitude (index qi, 0 to 3 for x y z w) is dropped after flipping the sign so that it is positive, and the other three, in x y z w order with qi skipped, are round(c / 0.70710678 * 32767); the dropped component is sqrt(max(0, 1 - sum of squares)).

asset_id.description: The first 16 hex characters of the asset file's sha256.

quat_xyzw.description: Unit quaternion, x y z w order (three.js).

asset.description: One content-addressed file (a GLB with embedded textures).

uri.description: Path relative to the site root.

license.description: SPDX licence identifier of the asset as shipped.

attribution.description: The credit line, exactly as on the credits page.

changes.description: What was changed from the upstream file. Required (non-empty) for every third-party asset.

brand_visible.description: Scanned objects only: whether a brand mark is visible. Hero shots use false only.

source.description: Where the asset came from: an upstream file pinned by sha256, or our own generator.

visual.description: An asset placed in a body frame (or the world frame for static_visuals). The right jaw is its own asset: scale is positive, never a mirror.

geom.description: A v1-style primitive or convex mesh geom (see rtt.sim.replay, version 1).

geoms.description: v1-style collision geoms, optional: the collision overlay.

meta.description: What was simulated. Writers may add further keys (metrics, phases).

geometry_id.description: sha256 over the training-part geometry hashes; null for designs without one (v1).

provenance.description: Where the replay came from; the burned-in caption is built from it.

code_version.description: Git commit of the code that ran the episode; '+dirty' if the tree was modified.

product_mode.description: True for product-mode episodes (options outside the scored space); clips then say 'product mode'.

overlays.description: Optional per-frame readouts in <stem>.ovl.bin: little-endian float16 [frames x channels], same frame clock as the poses.
